text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- The government has finalised banking laws to recover 140 billion rupees from the defaulters of nationalised commercial banks and development financial institutions.
- The Pakistan Commodity Traders Association has urged the government to withdraw subsidies on the supply of imported food items as these are hardly passed on to consumers.
- The government is likely to set up a special force to fight terrorism.
- Authorities have seized 5.8 tonnes of charas (hashish) near Rawalpindi.
- Customs officials have seized arms and cartridges near Karachi.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The government is considering a proposal to set up an oil refinery costing $1.5 billion, Pakistan's ambassador to Kuwait Mushtaque A. Mehar said.
- The Pakistan Sugar Mills Assocation has urged the government not to reduce customs duty on sugar import.
- Pakistan is likely to launch its own satellite for the Internet by the end of this year.
FINANCIAL POST
- An opposition leader in the Senate said the government plans to close 1,000 branches of nationalised banks.
THE NEWS
- A report of a law enforcing agency has alleged that religious schools are harbouring foreign elements fomenting sectarian violence in the country.
- President Farooq Leghari called for strengthening the intelligence network to check growing sectarian violence.
- A four-member enquiry committee has completed a report on the case of drug smuggling to the United States allegedly by two officers of the Pakistan Air Force.
THE MUSLIM

- The Ehtesab (accountability) Commission referred four more cases involving former petroleum minister Anwer Saifullah and ex-chairman of the Oil and Gas Development Authority, the late Riffat Askari, to the accountability bench of the Lahore High Court.
THE NATION
- Pakistan has received several proposals from foreign investors for development of a port at Gwadar, Balochistan.
- Pakistan's total revenues will fall far short of the amount required for debt servicing and defence spending in fiscal 1997-98.

- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif returned home after attending the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation summit in Male and an extraordinary summit session of the Economic Cooperation Organistaion in Ashgabad.
- Opposition members in Senate staged a walk-out to protest against "unfair" coverage on state-owned electronic media.
